top_story: Israeli strikes in Gaza on 23 August killed at least two people, including a four-year-old boy, underscoring that civilian exposure to lethal force remains a current condition rather than a closed phase of the war. That violence now sits alongside intensifying scrutiny of earlier incidents: Israel’s 20 August admission that its troops fired on the car in which Hind Rajab and six relatives were killed reopened one of the conflict’s most emblematic civilian deaths and forced a criminal investigation. By 24 August, findings that a hospital “double-tap” attack likely amounted to war crimes widened the focus from a single case to an apparent pattern affecting medics, journalists, and families seeking care. The cumulative effect is to deepen pressure on Israel not only over battlefield conduct but over the credibility of accountability mechanisms as Gaza’s civilian harm continues unabated.
